messages:
oncall-bot: Pager: LATENCY SLO ALERT - p99 streaming tail > 6s for /v1/stream
oncall-bot: Severity: P1
oncall-bot: Affected services: ingress-router (usw2), lb-ingress, streaming-proxy
oncall-bot: Trigger: p99 > 6s for last 4m. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/latency-tail
eli: I'm awake. pulling dashboards now. first spike at 16:18 UTC
mira: I'm grabbing routing decision logs and recent config pushes
samir: quick context: weight rollout to push traffic to model-v3 started earlier at 14:02
jordan: CS reports two EU customers saw streaming stalls ~16:20, raising support tickets
eli: metrics: p95 ~ 380ms, p99 ~ 6.8s; error rate normal. only streaming paths affected
mira: router decision logs show heavy concentration to shard-9 (hostgroup h9) in usw2
mira: counts: shard-9 41k, shard-3 2.4k, shard-12 1.6k. policy=weight-rollout, weight for shard-9=0.47
eli: that doesn't match the rollout plan. seed-based hashing should spread evenly
samir: check deploy history
deploy-bot: config-push 14:00 by infra-automation (id cfg-2026-04-02-881)
anya: oncall SRE here. we had a similar outage before when a single node used an old hash seed
mira: running quick host check:
```
for node in $(kubectl get pods -l app=router -o name); do kubectl exec $node -- cat /etc/router_seed || true; done
```
mira: found one router pod with seed=0x12b4, others 0x7d3f
samir: seed mismatch confirmed. that pod's older binary applied a legacy seed logic that bunched keys into shard-9
eli: impact path: that pod's decisions caused LB affinity to prefer h9, h9 overloaded -> KV misses + kernel slowpath -> streaming stalls and high tail
eli: immediate mitigation: 1) take offending router pod out of rotation; 2) revert weight rollout; 3) enable fallback routing for streaming; 4) confirm KV cache rebalance
jordan: cordon/drain command issued: `kubectl cordon router-usw2-9 && kubectl delete pod router-usw2-9 --grace-period=30`
opsbot: LB: router-usw2-9 removed from rotation
mira: after pod removal requests rebalanced, p99 down to ~1.5s within 45s
samir: rolling back weight change now: `infra-config rollback cfg-2026-04-02-881`
opsbot: rollback applied successfully. weights normalizing
eli: enabling eager-stream-fallback toggle: `infra-toggle streaming_short_circuit true`
opsbot: feature-flag streaming_short_circuit = TRUE
eli: p99 improved to ~700ms at 16:28 UTC
mira: KV cache hits improved from 64% -> 82% after spread
anya: handoff: I'm handing incident to @jordan for follow-up and postmortem ownership
jordan: will run cluster-wide binary version check and add postmortem notes
mira: root cause: config push + a single pod running an outdated router binary led to hash-seed drift -> weight skew -> hot shard saturation -> streaming tail latency. Missing canary/quarantine checks for routing weight changes
eli: customer impact: 4 customers in eu-west experienced streaming stalls (timeouts up to 12s) for ~10m window
jordan: mitigation summary: offending pod removed, rollout reverted, fallback enabled, customers notified. I'll produce writeup and action items
anya: action items:
- require router binary version match during config pushes (preflight)
- add safety: reject weight diffs that put >25% traffic on single shard
- canary: run a shard-distribution check in rollout pipeline
- seed-drift monitor: alert when node seed != cluster seed
samir: I'll open PRs for guardrails and seed detector; will assign to eng-runtime + eng-sre
eli: timeline entry created: https://redwood/incidents/2109987654
jordan: final: p99 6.8s -> 0.7s within ~10 minutes. marking mitigated; will lead postmortem
oncall-bot: Incident marked mitigated at 16:31 UTC. Keep thread for postmortem updates.
